thread:
kevin (runtime): Heads-up — saw a ~15% p99 regression on the Llama3-13B serving path after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. Repro on canary cluster.

kevin (runtime): Metrics: baseline p99 ~120ms -> canary p99 ~138ms, median unchanged. Throughput same.

tara (eng-ml): Ugh. Any profiling traces? looks like latency tail, might be batching edge-case.

oliver (perf): Pushed a quick perf trace to the canary host. Main findings: more time in attention kernel (attention_split_k) and a ~30% increase in device-to-device memcpy calls during the request.

oliver (perf): Snippet from nvprof / perf (condensed):
```
time  kernel           nsamples  total_ms
45.3  fused_matmul_v2   1024      18.2
32.1  attention_split_k 2048      27.6  <-- up from 18ms
10.9  kv_copy           512       6.4   <-- memcpy spikes
```

kevin (runtime): Interesting — selector started preferring attention_split_k for long-prefix batches. We changed the cost heuristic to favor lower memory at cost of compute. Maybe the batching shapes now force split_k.

sara (oncall): I also saw more KV-evict logs on the canary: frequent small evictions and re-writes. Could be chat template + prefix padding interaction causing low cache hit rate.

tara (eng-ml): Chat templates? Are we zero-padding prefixes differently for Llama3? If prefix tokens aren't treated as cacheable, we lose reuse. Any example request payload?

kevin (runtime): Example request that repros reliably: 1) user prompt with 350 tokens + system prompt 80 tokens (we apply chat template prefix pad to 512) -> batching groups with short later queries. Because of prefix pad we end up with longer seq_len in batch leading selector -> split_k path. Also KV cache stores per-head slices sized for head_dim=64 and hidden_size=8192 spec.

oliver (perf): Additional traces show head_dim mismatch for a migrated Llama3 variant: hidden_size=8192 but head_dim 64 vs expected 128 in some kernels. That causes extra reshapes and copies.

kevin (runtime): So multiple factors: kernel selector cost weight change, chat-prefix padding inflating seq_len, and head_dim/hidden_size kernel mismatch causing memcpy. Any quick mitigations?

tara (eng-ml): Short-term: revert selector heuristic change on canary (roll back flag). Also reduce prefix padding to minimal for chat template in canary routing; we can do per-model override.

kevin (runtime): I'll flip selector flag to old weights and set per-model override to disable aggressive prefix pad for Llama3-13B. Patch coming.

oliver (perf): Proposed longer-term: update selector to include an estimated KV memcpy cost term: cost = flops_cost + mem_copy_cost * alpha. Alpha learned per-model from profiling. Also add a fast-path fused attention when head_dim==expected to avoid reshapes.

sara (oncall): I'll add alerts for KV-evict rate and memcpy bytes/sec so we catch this earlier. CI-bot can we add a perf regression check on p99 for the kernel-selector change?

ci-bot: @kevin created perf-check job "selector-p99-smoke" (jobs/selector-p99-smoke) — results will post to this thread. :gear:

kevin (runtime): Plan: (1) rollback selector weights on canary (in 10m), (2) reduce chat prefix padding override, (3) run perf-check job, (4) instrument memcpy/KV-evict alerts, (5) follow-up work to expand selector cost model + fused kernel fast-path.

tara (eng-ml): +1. Also let's add a small unit-test synthetic that simulates chat-template + prefix pad + mixed short queries to capture future regressions.

oliver (perf): I'll put up a PR with the fused attention patch and a selector alpha tweak. Will include microbench harness and repro script.

kevin (runtime): Thanks — ping me when PRs are up. If rollback fixes p99 we can schedule a careful re-eval of the selector change with new cost term.

sara (oncall): Rolling back now. Will report back in 5–10m.

ci-bot: perf-check job queued (selector-p99-smoke). Estimated runtime: 12m.

kevin (runtime): tl;dr: regression root cause = selector heuristics + inflated seq shapes from chat prefix padding + occasional head_dim mismatch causing memcpy; mitigations deployed to canary and follow-ups tracked.
